summary: Repaired PREREG-S2.md with four retractions, then designed one new exact placement. Retractions: rho(C1)-A1 is not a genuine cross edge, since A1 = rho(A2) makes it the transport of the internal edge C1-A2 (B-internal); the K5-with-subdivided-edge example is false (4-colourable, and adding uv keeps it 5-colourable) - the correct gadget is K6 minus an edge, unrealizable since it contains K4; 'a fixed-point rotation prevents pair separation' has no proof and is withdrawn; overlap indexing corrected to c1(A1) = c2(A2), c1(B-) = c2(B+) with preimage map rho-inverse. Then PREREG-S3.md: for an edge {a,b} of H and any vertex r, with d1 = a-r, d2 = b-r and n the unit perpendicular of b-a (unit because a,b are adjacent), tau = (d1+d2)/2 + s(sqrt3/2)n is the apex of the equilateral triangle on d1d2, so |a-(r+tau)| = |b-(r+tau)| = 1 by equilateral closure, all in K(sqrt3) - two cross edges by construction, genuine only if the exact tests tau not in D(H) and a-tau, b-tau not in V(H) pass. Stated the missing condition (G4): a k=5 pair needs four exclusions, at most two from the common-neighbour channel, so two more must attach to the same pair; S3 does not achieve this and I say so rather than overselling it.
verified_results: GRADE [P] Retraction C1 of PREREG-S2.md: the pair (rho(C1), A1) is not a new constraint. Because A1 = rho(A2), the pair is the rho-image of the internal edge C1-A2 and is therefore internal to copy B. A genuine cross edge requires one endpoint in V(M)\I and the other in rho(V(M))\I; section 3 of S2 exhibits none, so S2's claimed cross-edge mechanism is void.

GRADE [P] Retraction C2: the abstract example 'K5 with edge uv subdivided by w' is false. The subdivided graph is 4-colourable (u and v share a colour, the other three take three colours, w reuses one) and adding uv is still 5-colourable (w is not adjacent to those three, so it may reuse a colour). The correct standard gadget is K6 minus one edge: 5-colourable with u,v sharing a colour, and adding uv gives K6, which is not 5-colourable. It is geometrically unrealizable because u together with three others forms a K4.

GRADE [P] Retraction C3: nothing proves that a fixed-point isometry prevents the union's colouring family from separating pairs; the only defensible differences from a translation are bookkeeping (overlap size, preimage map). Separation must be measured.

GRADE [P] Retraction C4 / corrected invariants: with c2 indexed by original M-vertices the overlap equations are c1(K)=c2(K), c1(A1)=c2(A2), c1(B-)=c2(B+), and the shared-vertex preimage map is rho-inverse restricted to the overlap: K to K, A1 to A2, B- to B+.

GRADE [P] PREREG-S3 construction: for an edge {a,b} of H and a vertex r, with d1=a-r, d2=b-r and n = R90(b-a) a unit vector, tau = (d1+d2)/2 + s(sqrt3/2)n satisfies |tau - d1| = |tau - d2| = 1 (equilateral triangle on d1d2), hence |a-(r+tau)| = |b-(r+tau)| = 1. Coordinates lie in K(sqrt3); the construction is exact, needs no search, and exhibits two unit pairs whose membership in class 'genuine cross' is decided by two exact tests.

GRADE [P] The class decomposition and the missing condition: unit pairs of a translate-glued union split into A-internal, B-internal, overlap-incidence and genuine cross; only the last couples the two colourings, and overlap incidence is inherited. (G4) is stated: at k=5 forcing a pair equal needs four excluded colours, at most two come from the common-neighbour channel (capped at two vertices in the plane), so a translation must supply two further exclusions for the same pair. S3 supplies two cross edges at one translated vertex and therefore does not meet (G4); this is stated rather than glossed.
conjectures: The closed 1048-vertex union's 184 cross edges were never split by class, so part of that budget may have been overlap incidence; the split is the first thing any re-analysis of it should report.

Two isolated cross edges cannot meet (G4), which asks for four exclusions attached to one pair; the next design should therefore aim at a small, exactly-checkable configuration where a single cross vertex is simultaneously at unit distance from four vertices of the other copy whose colours are forced distinct - the planar cap (no K4) means those four must be spread across two copies.

If S3's exact tests pass and its colouring family still separates every nonedge, the informative negative is that guaranteed cross edges of the 'equilateral apex' type are too sparse to force; the natural next step is a symmetric placement gluing at two apexes at once so that a pair receives two exclusions from each side.
